title: CoreWeave Just Landed a Multibillion-Dollar AI Deal. How to Play CRWV Stock.
excerpt: CoreWeave’s multibillion-dollar deal with Hudson River Trading adds a major AI customer and strengthens the case for its growing cloud infrastructure busines...
content_html:
CoreWeave (CRWV) has just landed another major customer for its artificial intelligence infrastructure. The AI cloud provider announced a multiyear, multibillion-dollar agreement with Hudson River Trading, one of the world's leading quantitative trading firms, to build a next-generation AI research platform on CoreWeave's cloud. 

The deal is important because HRT is an unusually demanding customer. Its trading models rely on massive computing power, speed, and low-latency infrastructure. HRT will use CoreWeave's platform, including NVIDIA (NVDA) Vera Rubin NVL72 systems and Spectrum-X networking, for AI-driven trading research and model development.

That provides another strong validation of CoreWeave's technology. But investors also have to consider CRWV's volatility, elevated valuation, and enormous capital requirements.

CRWV Stock Is Still a Wild Ride

CRWV stock has been extremely volatile in 2026. The stock is down about 16% over three months despite recovering more than 47% from its July low of $60. Over the past year, CRWV is down roughly 4%, after reaching a 52-week high of $153.20 in October 2025.

The volatility shows a tug-of-war between explosive AI demand and concerns about how much CoreWeave must spend to capture it. Shares jumped more than 14% after the company's latest earnings report, but the stock remains well below its 2025 high.

The Hudson River deal could help change that narrative because it adds another sophisticated customer and reinforces demand for CoreWeave's increasingly scarce compute capacity.

Hudson River Deal Strengthens CoreWeave's AI Position

The biggest takeaway from the HRT announcement is not simply the multibillion-dollar contract. It is the type of customer CoreWeave just won.

Quantitative trading firms demand extremely high-performance computing because even tiny improvements in speed and model performance can matter. By choosing CoreWeave for its next-generation research platform, HRT is effectively validating the company's infrastructure for one of the most technically demanding AI workloads. 

The timing is also notable. CoreWeave finished Q2 with a $104.2 billion revenue backlog, up from $99.4 billion in Q1, and added more than $25 billion in additional commitments early in Q3.
